Minnesota's win total sits at 8.5, and oddsmakers have posted several intriguing season-long player props. Bet on the NFL and more at DraftKings and get $200 in bonus bets when you spend $5+: Best Vikings player prop bets for 2026 Justin Jefferson Over 1,150.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Jefferson barely crossed 1,000 yards last year after catching passes from J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer. Minnesota featured the NFL's fifth-worst dropback EPA in 2025, and with Murray in town, that efficiency is likely to improve. The man who won the 2022 Offensive Player of the Year Award has fallen below 1150.5 receiving yards twice in six seasons - 2023, when he missed seven games due to a hamstring injury, and last year because of quarterback struggles and inconsistency. The prop asks for just 103 additional yards compared to last year across the entire schedule. Jefferson should be capable of clearing the number if Murray wins the starting job and restores even part of Minnesota's downfield efficiency. In 2024, he produced 1,533 yards and led the NFL with 28 receptions of at least 20 yards. Bet on the NFL with the BetMGM bonus code CBSSPORTS for up to $1,500 in bonus bets: Aaron Jones Under 875.5 Scrimmage Yards (-125) Jones and Jordan Mason are tentatively scheduled to share the RB1 workload in Minnesota, making the 875.5 yards from scrimmage a large ask, especially for a running back who will turn 32 in December. Thirty-two-year-old running backs don't typically improve each year, and Jones tallied just 747 yards from scrimmage in 2025. He missed five games due to injury, and given his track record, it would not be strange for Jones to miss more time in 2026. Mason also outproduced Jones in 2025 despite sharing the Vikings' backfield. Mason finished with 809 yards from scrimmage, including 758 rushing yards at 4.8 per carry. Overall, Mason already surpassed Jones in carries, rushing yards, total scrimmage yards, and yards per attempt last season. The under is a wager that Minnesota preserves that committee structure rather than returning the 31-year-old Jones to his 2024 workhorse role. Bet on the NFL at FanDuel Sportsbook and get up to $350 in bonus bets : Dallas Turner Over 7.5 Sacks (-125) The Vikings traded Jonathan Greenard and a 7th-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles in April for two 3rd-rounders. After two years behind Greenard on Minnesota's depth chart, it's showtime for Turner, who the Vikings acquired in a rather expensive trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2024. Turner already recorded 8 sacks, 15 quarterback hits, 11 tackles for loss, and 4 forced fumbles in 2025. He also generated 42 pressures with a 12% pass-rush win rate. He does not need a breakout to cash this ticket; he merely needs to approximate his 2025 production. If Turner could accumulate 8 sacks as the OLB3 last season, clearing 6.5 in 2026 as the OLB1 or OLB2 should be elementary. Claim $365 in bonus bets with a $10 bet by signing up for bet365 Sportsbook here : Jordan Addison Over 4.5 Receiving TDs (+110) Minnesota's recent receiver split has been straightforward: Jefferson supplies the volume yardage, while Addison provides the touchdowns. If Addison wishes to remain the paydirt merchant, he must score more than four touchdowns. Addison has averaged one receiving touchdown every 2.1 career games, a rate that projects to more than eight across a 17-game season. The wager asks him for only five after his first two NFL campaigns produced 10 and nine. He also scored seven touchdowns over the final eight games of 2024, demonstrating how productive he can become when Minnesota's passing offense functions properly. Improved quarterback play - whether supplied by Murray or McCarthy - would give Addison a strong chance to rebound in the touchdown column. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. Moore is coming off two lackluster seasons by his standards, but a new environment and the opportunity to play with Josh Allen may have created the perfect recipe for an excellent buy-low opportunity. Moore has been seen smiling throughout training camp as he enters 2026 in a dramatically different situation after being traded from Chicago to Buffalo. Instead of playing in an environment where something was clearly not right personally and in a Ben Johnson offense where his target share declined significantly, Moore now gets to catch passes from a former MVP quarterback while reuniting with Joe Brady , his former offensive coordinator in Carolina. The biggest reason to bet Moore’s over is simple: Allen is without a doubt the best quarterback Moore has ever had passing him the ball. Moore has spent most of his career dealing with inconsistent quarterback situations, yet he has still exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in four seasons. He enters his ninth season averaging more than 1,000 receiving yards per season. Moore is also a huge upgrade at the wide receiver position for Allen. The Bills have not produced a 1,000-yard-wide receiver in either of the previous two seasons since Stefon Diggs ’ departure, while their average target depth ranked last in the NFL in 2025. Moore doesn't need an unreasonable target share to beat his season-long receiving-yardage line, but he should command a target share over 20% given the receiver depth in Buffalo. The Bills entered the 2024 season with a new slogan: Everybody Eats. Sean McDermott tried to spin that into a positive after the Bills parted ways with Diggs. However, targets are earned. The “Everybody Eats” slogan was admitting to everyone what was glaringly obvious: There wasn’t an alpha target earner on the roster. In an interview, Ian Rapoport talked about Moore as a breakout candidate for the upcoming fantasy season, but fantasy gamers should be aware that “the Buffalo Bills like to spread the ball around.” Again, this is a mythical statement and is a byproduct of a lackluster receiving room. Diggs was a member of the Buffalo Bills from 2020 to 2023. In those four years, he led all NFL receivers in receptions, was second in targets, and had 28.0% of the Bills' total team targets over that span. Before last season, Moore had four consecutive seasons in which he had over 26% of his team’s targets. In 2021, Brady’s final season as the Carolina Panthers offensive coordinator, Moore had 28.3% of the team's targets and 40.2% of the team’s total air yards. In that season, Moore caught passes from Cam Newton , Sam Darnold , and PJ Walker and still exceeded 1,150 receiving yards. The projections in the Sharp Football Analysis Draft Kit are bullish on Moore joining the Bills. Our projections have Moore projected for 83 receptions and more than 1,100 receiving yards, well over the season-long yardage prop. One of the biggest risks of betting season-long overs is injury. Moore has played every game in the past five seasons and has played 15 or more games in all eight seasons to start his career. Moore has played through injury in the past, which helps give him the opportunity to continue to accumulate volume over the full season. The market may be overreacting to Moore’s 2025 season and overconfident that his decline is age-related. In addition to our projections supporting the over, in the Wide Receiver Trends article, Rich Hribar highlighted that when searching for wide receivers to exceed expectations, one of the more common hits comes from players changing situations, making Moore a solid bet this season. Loveland was selected in the top 10 of the 2025 NFL Draft and entered the league with an elite tight end profile and skill set. Loveland started his rookie season slowly as he missed part of training camp with an injury and played a part-time role in the Bears offense in the opening months of the season. He opened his rookie season with just 5 receptions and 54 yards in the opening five games while he was still establishing himself within Ben Johnson ‘s offense and managing an injury. Loveland’s role and production accelerated dramatically as the season progressed. He finished the regular season and playoffs with four consecutive double-digit target games, including a 15-target game in the Bears' playoff victory against the Packers. The late-season production provides a much better indication of what Loveland could look like with a full-time role throughout the entire season. Loveland shared the field with rookie wide receiver Luther Burden for 173 passing plays and generated more targets, air yards, and receiving yards than the hyped second-year receiver. Both Loveland and Burden are projected for increasing roles in Year 2. However, Loveland may still be overlooked. Loveland led the Bears in receiving yards despite only being on the field for 63.8% of the team's dropbacks. With the Bears trading D.J. In the final five weeks of the regular season, the Bears had multiple tight ends on the field on 56.9% of the offensive plays. The increase of 13 personnel benefited Loveland the most as he averaged 3.34 yards per route and had 32.4% of the team's targets with three tight ends on the field. Johnson recently did an interview in which he stated that he wants the 2026 Bears to be the highest-scoring offense ever . The Bears have the seventh-most difficult strength of schedule in 2026, after the ninth-easiest last season. Injuries to Coby Bryant and Kyler Gordon are concerning for a defense which is not particularly deep with talent in the secondary, which could force the Bears into more shootouts, boosting Loveland’s ceiling. Including the playoffs, Loveland averaged 9.9 air yards per target, which led all tight ends in the league, and gained 20 or more yards on 21.4% of his receptions. The ability to operate deeper down the field and create explosives means that a relatively modest increase in targets can produce substantial increases in yardage. Another important component in Loveland’s ascent is Caleb Williams . Williams registered an off-target throw on 15.9% of his passes targeted at the rookie tight end last season. Entering his third season in the NFL and second season with Johnson, Williams appears more comfortable running the offense than a year ago. Even a slight improvement in accuracy benefits Loveland. Given the way his role expanded throughout 2025, the 2026 season could be the year Loveland goes from promising rookie to legitimate NFL receiving weapon who is mentioned in the same sentence as Brock Bowers and Trey McBride when discussing the league’s high-upside tight ends. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Opening-week workloads point us toward a few early NFL player props for Week 2 Derrick Henry leads a pair of rushing props coming off heavy Week 1 usage Keep reading for our three early NFL props to target in Week 2, starting with Thursday night One week of football doesn’t settle much, but it does show how teams plan to use their best players. For early Week 2 props, I want players with a defined role and a number they can beat without repeating their best game. That starts with a Bills quarterback hosting a Detroit defense that just allowed 410 passing yards, then moves to a pair of rushing props driven by workload. Here are the NFL props I’m targeting for Week 2. NFL Week 2 Player Props to Target Player Prop Projected Line Josh Allen (BUF) Over Passing Yards 220.5 Derrick Henry (BAL) Over Rushing Yards 78.5 Caleb Williams (CHI) Over Rushing Yards 20.5 These projected targets are not posted sportsbook lines. NFL Player Prop Pick: Josh Allen Passing Yards Josh Allen didn’t need big volume to carve up the Texans in Week 1. He completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions in a 36-31 win at Houston. He spread the ball around, too. DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid combined for 230 receiving yards, so Allen isn’t leaning on one target to move the offense. That makes Buffalo a tough team to slow down through the air. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to Tyler Shough in their opener. He went 35-of-56 with three touchdowns and two interceptions, and Detroit still escaped with a 31-30 overtime win. That yardage came on a heavy workload, and Allen doesn’t need anything close to it. He threw for 334 yards on 29 attempts, which is 27 fewer than Shough. A 220.5 target leaves plenty of room. Allen can fall well short of his Week 1 performance and still cash the over, and he gets the Lions at home on Thursday night. Early Bet: Josh Allen over 220.5 passing yards NFL Player Prop Pick: Derrick Henry Rushing Yards Baltimore gave Derrick Henry plenty of work in the opener. He carried 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns in a 41-23 win at Indianapolis. For a yardage prop, the carries matter more than the scores. The Ravens kept feeding Henry in a game they won comfortably, and that kind of volume can get him over this number even if the big runs don’t show up. New Orleans just spent an overtime game trying to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs, without much luck. Gibbs ran 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. Now the Saints have to deal with Henry. Henry averaged 6.0 yards per carry against the Colts, but this bet doesn’t need that kind of efficiency. Even at 4.0 per carry, 20 attempts would put him over the target. If Baltimore gives him anything close to his Week 1 volume at home on Sunday, 78.5 is a number I’m happy to bet the over on. Early Bet: Derrick Henry over 78.5 rushing yards NFL Player Prop Pick: Caleb Williams Rushing Yards Caleb Williams ran a lot more than usual in Week 1. He carried 10 times for 65 yards and two touchdowns, well above the 4.5 carries per game he averaged last season. That’s the kind of usage you want to see for a quarterback rushing prop. His 2025 numbers already support this bet. Williams finished with 77 carries for 388 yards and three touchdowns over 17 games, which works out to 22.8 rushing yards per game. The 20.5 target sits below that average before Week 1 even enters the picture. The carries could settle back down, and that’s fine. Williams averaged 5.0 yards per carry last season, so he doesn’t need double-digit attempts to reach the low 20s. With the Vikings visiting Chicago on Sunday, I’m taking the over at 20.5. His average last season was already above this target, and he ran more often in the opener. Last season, I went 39-27 (59.1%) and 42-19 (68.9%) in 2024 for an overall success rate of 63.8% on my weekly props pieces. Let's get into my NFL player props for Week 2, including picks for Steelers vs Patriots , Seahawks vs Cardinals, and Dolphins vs 49ers. Download the Action Network app now for more picks and analysis! NFL Player Props — Week 2 Aaron Rodgers Under 0.5 Interceptions (-135 at bet365; -139 at DraftKings; -141 Caesars) Jeremiyah Love Longest Rush Under 11.5 Yards (-109 at DraftKings) Christian McCaffrey Under 43.5 Receiving Yards (-115 at bet365) Steelers vs Patriots Player Prop: Aaron Rodgers Interceptions I'm pretty shocked at this price given Rodgers hasn't been an interception machine at all in his career, even recently. Since he joined the Steelers, Rodgers has seven interceptions in 17 games, for a rate of 0.41 per game, throwing just 14 turnover-worthy plays (TWPs) in that time, which equates to pretty neutral interception luck since just north of 50% of TWPs are picked. That jives with my model, as he has a -0.18 per-game "gift" average compared to league average, so when he throws defended passes, they are ones that are still difficult to be picked, showing his elite ball placement. His matchup against New England is solid too. Last year the Patriots had 10 picks in 17 regular season games. Yes, they had four against Stroud in a playoff game, but it was clear Stroud was totally rattled in cold conditions. Overall, the Patriots ranked as a slightly below-average defense in passes defended and interceptions, and so far in 2026 they haven't shown anything to make me think much differently. My Luck Rankings Dashboard is showing Rodgers with a projected 0.44 interceptions and just a 35.7% chance of having one. That means this is good to around -180, but to be safe, I'd play this to just -150. Pick: Aaron Rodgers Under 0.5 Interceptions (-135) Seahawks vs Cardinals Player Prop: Jeremiyah Love Rush Yards In his NFL debut, Love had 11 carries for 41 yards with a long of 18 yards. That means, outside of that carry, he averaged 2.3 yards per carry against the Chargers, who were an explosive play machine against opposing RBs last year, ranking 25th in stopping explosive runs to running backs. Now he faces a Seahawks defense that dominates on the ground, ranking first last year. Yes, they allowed Rhamondre Stevenson to hit a long of 12 yards, but it took him 18 attempts to do so. Love is a fantastic talent, but the attempts likely aren't going to be there, as he had 11 in a heavily leading game script in Week 1. Despite Drew Lock being at QB for the Seahawks, I think this will be a more neutral-to-Seahawks-leading script, and it's reflected in Love's rushing attempt line as books have him at 10.5 attempts, heavily juiced to the under. Yes, I know Ty Okada is out, and Nick Emmanwori is questionable, but they were the same status in Week 1 and Seattle shut down Rhamondre Stevenson on what projects to be around eight more carries than Love should have. I'd play this to -130 or so. Picks: Jeremiyah Love Longest Rush Under 11.5 Yards (-109 at DraftKings) Dolphins vs 49ers Player Prop: Christian McCaffrey Receiving Yards When the 49ers are 9.5-point favorites or more (within a half point of a field goal plus a touchdown), McCaffrey has an average of 37.5 receiving yards, but a median of just 30.5 in twelve games on 4.8 targets per game. In those twelve games, he cleared 40.5 yards just four times, but in each of those four he went for more than 65 yards. Trim that to 12.5-point favorites (within a half point of a touchdown plus two field goals) and he averages 35.9 yards with a median of just 27 on 4.0 targets across seven games. Miami got gashed by Ashton Jeanty last week, but that was in a game with no Brock Bowers in a game that was close partway through the third quarter. San Francisco has so many more weapons and projects to be in a bigger blowout that there's enough opportunity to spread the ball around here that McCaffrey's receiving volume probably isn't going to be massive. After all, as I mentioned above, he's averaged just four targets in heavily favored games. I'm projecting a median in the mid 30s, but there's always a chance CMC has a 70+ yard receiving game like he's done in two of the seven games he's played as a 49er as a super-heavy favorite. However, those were the only two heavily favored games he cleared 40.5 receiving yards as a 49er. Based on his splits, he's likely to stay under, but if he clears it, you could do worse than throwing a sprinkle on 60+ or 70+ alt receiving yards.
